rotational-inertia.def: How hard it is to change an object’s rotation about an axis: I = Σmr² for point masses, in kg·m². It depends on the mass and how far that mass is from the axis. Also called moment of inertia.

mass-distribution.def: How an object’s mass is spread out relative to an axis. The same mass placed farther from the axis gives a larger rotational inertia.

parallel-axis.def: I = I_cm + Md²: the rotational inertia about any axis equals the inertia about a parallel axis through the center of mass plus the total mass times the square of the distance between the axes.
